The order creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, directs it to report to the President within the statutory period, bars changes in the disputed conditions while the board and the following period run, and says the board terminates upon submission of its report. Legal reading: a report date is a deadline, not an end. Holding the order blocked rather than recording a deadline as an end, or a conjectured date, which the project rule forbids.

research_rationale: EO 13004 of May 17, 1996 (Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between Certain Railroads Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and Their Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations), read in full in the held Federal Register text (61 FR 25771, Federal Register of May 22, 1996; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row. The order creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, directs it to report to the President within the statutory period, bars changes in the disputed conditions while the board and the following period run, and says the board terminates upon submission of its report. Legal reading: a report date is a deadline, not an end. The held sources do not show when the board actually submitted its report, and no held instrument revokes or supersedes this order by number or by terms; the 1986 general emergency-board order predates it and cannot be a later event. Holding the order blocked rather than recording a deadline as an end, or a conjectured date, which the project rule forbids.
